metadata.note: Wilmington, NC's other historic rail lines, radiating out to complete its status as a 19th-century rail hub, alongside the Wilmington and Weldon Railroad already on this map (see wilmington_weldon_railroad.geojson, north toward Goldsboro/Rocky Mount/Weldon and on to Richmond/Washington/Baltimore/Philadelphia/New York via the Petersburg Railroad and connecting lines). Four more routes: south and west to Florence (and onward to Charleston/Columbia/Augusta) via the former Wilmington & Manchester/Wilmington, Columbia & Augusta; northwest to Sanford (and on to Fayetteville, Greensboro, Mt. Airy) via the former Cape Fear & Yadkin Valley Railway; northeast to New Bern via the former Wilmington, Onslow and East Carolina/Wilmington, New Bern and Norfolk; and west to Hamlet (and on to Charlotte and Rutherfordton) via the former Wilmington, Charlotte and Rutherford/Carolina Central Railway, later a core Seaboard Air Line route -- Hamlet itself became known as the 'Hub of the Seaboard' by 1936, with five lines and ~30 daily passenger departures. All four ended up feeding Wilmington's Union Station, whose last passenger train of any kind departed in 1968 (per the same 1960 ACL headquarters relocation to Jacksonville, FL and general Wilmington rail decline documented in wilmington_weldon_railroad.geojson) -- used here as a consistent, approximate end date for all four lines' passenger service since exact discontinuation dates per line are not individually sourced. GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: Florence, Sanford, and Hamlet lines are real-traced through OpenStreetMap active/abandoned-rail data (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search), with several short hand-placed bridges (a few km each) where Overpass found no connected path even including abandoned ways. The New Bern line is entirely hand-placed waypoints through real towns (Jacksonville, Pollocksville) -- this rural coastal route appears heavily fragmented/removed in OSM today, with no usable connected remnant found even a hundred-plus km in the right direction.

properties.company: Wilmington, Charlotte and Rutherford Railroad / Carolina Central Railway / Seaboard Air Line
properties.line: Seaboard Air Line: Wilmington – Hamlet (toward Charlotte/Rutherfordton)

segments.note: The Wilmington and Charlotte Railroad Co. (soon renamed Wilmington, Charlotte and Rutherford, WC&R) began construction Jan 1 1857 at Navassa near Wilmington; reached Rockingham (adjacent to Hamlet) by Apr 1861, 112 miles, before the Civil War halted work. Construction resumed 1870; foreclosed 1873 and reorganized as the Carolina Central Railway, which completed the full 267-mile Wilmington-Rutherfordton line by 1887 and came under Seaboard & Roanoke (future Seaboard Air Line) control; frequency estimated, unsourced
